title: Protest in Portland rallies voters on No Kings Day ahead of midterms
seoTitle: Portland rally for midterms on No Kings Day

tea.why: Protesters gathered to encourage early voting in the upcoming midterm elections and oppose the policies of the administration and Senator Susan Collins.
tea.want: Participants demanded the election of Maine Democrats and the removal of five-term Republican incumbent Senator Susan Collins.
tea.changed: Oct 17: About 400 people gathered in Deering Oaks park in Portland featuring speakers including Elizabeth Warren, Troy Jackson, and Hannah Pingree.

summary: Approximately 400 people gathered in Deering Oaks park in Portland, Maine, on Saturday to participate in a rally coinciding with the fourth national No Kings Day, held just weeks before the midterm elections. Organized by Indivisible Greater Portland, the event focused on encouraging early voting and supporting Democratic candidates, including gubernatorial candidate Hannah Pingree and U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson, alongside guest speaker U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts. Speakers criticized the administration and U.S. Senator Susan Collins, addressing topics such as healthcare, foreign policy, and economic challenges. Attendees held signs calling for changes in Senate representation and rejecting political corruption.
demands: Vote early in the midterm elections
response: No official government or police response reported in the sources.

updates.text: About 400 people gathered at Deering Oaks in Portland for a No Kings Day rally organized by Indivisible Greater Portland.
